title: For an irreducible subset and a finite union of locally closed subsets the three density conditions are equivalent

core_obligations: The trivial implication and the reduction: (1) implies (2) is clear, and assuming (2) the proof notes that the intersection of the constructible set with the irreducible subset is a finite union of locally closed pieces (proof lines 3066-3068).

Irreducibility forces one piece to be dense: since the ambient subset is irreducible, one of the pieces is dense, and because that piece is locally closed it is then open dense, which gives (1) (proof lines 3068-3072).
The generic-point form: if the ambient subset has a generic point, density of the intersection is equivalent to the generic point lying in the constructible set (proof lines 3072-3075).
Conclusion: the equivalences of the statement (proof line 3075).
proof_roadmap: (1) ⇒ (2) 显然；设 (2)，则 E ∩ Z 是有限多个局部闭子集之并。
由 Z 不可约，其中一个必在 Z 中稠密；又因它是局部闭的，故在 Z 中开稠密，得 (1)。若 Z 有 generic point ξ，则稠密性等价于 ξ ∈ E，即 (3)。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the equivalence of three density conditions for a constructible subset against an irreducible subset (author lemma at source lines 3047-3063, label lemma-generic-point-in-constructible), with the generic-point formulation as the third condition. The proof (source lines 3065-3076) has its content in the step from density to openness: the intersection is a finite union of locally closed pieces, irreducibility selects one dense piece, and local closedness of that piece upgrades density to open density (proof lines 3066-3072); the equivalence with the generic-point condition is then immediate (proof lines 3072-3075). The lemma is used throughout the constructible-sets section. H2.
